idea: Use row-slide insertion moves. In the best layout, find a maximal straight line of edges spanning the square (a guillotine seam) and slide everything on one side by δ to open a strip. Fill the strip with a column of equal small squares, then re-solve the compaction LP so neighbours absorb the loss. Choose δ analytically as the breakpoint where the added count's sum exceeds the shrinkage cost.
